findings.evidence: finish(): on OSError from terminate/_wait_empty it returns contained=False without appending the job to _OPEN_JOBS (and without closing it, so KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE does not fire); precheck() iterates only _OPEN_JOBS. run_cmd discards finish()'s result. Probe /tmp/uri_review_R1/probe_precheck.py with a fake API (query fails once, job still has 2 active): 'gate finish: contained False ... job not verified' then 'job 1 still has 2 active; next worker precheck: {contained: True, killed: 0}'. A gate whose job could not be created or assigned is likewise invisible to precheck, unlike the Linux sweep, which catches any orphan. Needs a kernel32 failure on a valid handle, or a per-command job failure, so the trigger is unlikely.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep every created job in _OPEN_JOBS whatever finish() does, and keep a sticky 'uncontained since last precheck' flag (set by any finish() or spawn() with contained=False) that makes the next precheck() return contained=False.
findings.title: Windows: a job whose termination/accounting query fails (or a command that ran without a job) is never re-checked by precheck(), so the next worker can be reported contained

findings.evidence: `git remote get-url <name>` returns the fetch URL; `git push <remote>` uses remote.<name>.pushurl / url.*.pushInsteadOf if set. The post-push ls-remote (fetch URL) stops a false INTEGRATED, but the candidate is pushed to the other repository.
findings.suggested_fix: Also require `git remote get-url --push --all <name>` to normalise to canonical_url, else BLOCKED REMOTE.
findings.title: canonical_remote() checks only the fetch URL; the integration push uses pushurl/pushInsteadOf, which may point at another repository

findings.evidence: Probe /tmp/uri_review_R1/norm.py: _norm_url('github.com/sche004-cyber/Uri') == _norm_url('https://github.com/sche004-cyber/Uri') -> True, although git treats that remote URL as a local relative directory. './x' resolves to os.getcwd()/x, not relative to the repository.
findings.suggested_fix: Only apply the host/path regex to URLs with a scheme or scp form (user@host:path); treat everything else as a local path resolved against cfg['repo'].
findings.title: _norm_url treats a bare relative path 'github.com/owner/Uri' as the canonical URL, and resolves a relative canonical_url against the driver's working directory

findings.evidence: init(): without baseline.remote_branch it runs `rev-parse --verify <ref>`, e.g. 'origin/integration/git-sync-20261008' (the pre-DL2 TEMPLATE form), reading a remote-tracking ref by name. load_config does not reject it. Mitigated by the 'expect' SHA and by rev-parse failing when the ref is missing (an error, not 'no baseline').
findings.suggested_fix: For non-DEVTEST milestones, require baseline.remote_branch, or refuse a baseline.ref under refs/remotes/ that does not belong to the canonical remote.
findings.title: The old baseline.ref form '<remote>/<branch>' is still accepted for real milestones and resolved by remote name, not checked against canonical_url
